name: Rainbow Warrior
imitates: A small midge or baetis nymph with an iridescent pearl-tinsel body and rainbow thorax; Lance Egan's flashy tungsten-bead dropper for cold-weather and tailwater fishing.
recipe: Stub end of the pearl tinsel

steps.text: Slide the bead to the eye, start the thread behind it, and lay a thread base back to the bend.
Peel about six pheasant tail fibers, even the tips, and tie them in at the bend about half a shank long.
Wrap forward over the butt ends to just behind the bead and clip the excess.
Tie in a strip of pearl tinsel behind the bead, wrap back over it to the tail base, then return the thread to the front for a smooth, slightly tapered base.
Wrap the tinsel forward in slightly overlapping turns to the bead and tie it off with a couple of tight thread turns.
Fold the leftover tinsel back over the top of the abdomen, tie it down flat, and wrap the thread back to just in front of the halfway point.
Dub a round rainbow thorax from the back of the bead to the base of the wing case and back again.
Pull the tinsel forward over the thorax and tie it down tightly at the back edge of the bead.
Fold the tinsel stub back over the wing case and bind it down so it cannot pull out, then clip the excess close to the bead.
Whip finish and clip the thread. The finished fly.
